CHE, use your RAG/pgvector system for this repair. You already have server/cloudflare/vector_memory.js with retrieveVectorContext(), and worker.js dispatchChange already retrieves vector context before prepareSelfUpdate. Use that retrieved memory to pull prior coding lessons, source locations, and earlier failure context before each repair attempt. But do not rely on RAG alone for repo state: for the current push failure, query GitHub repository metadata and resolve the live default branch/ref before creating or pushing a repair branch. I verified Vondada/chey-app currently reports default_branch = main. If your push path says 'base branch not found', treat that as a branch-resolution bug: refresh repo metadata, verify refs/heads/main exists, discard any stale/nonexistent base value, then create the new branch from the current main SHA and push there. Continue the existing Chat/self-repair task after that. Report vector_memory_status/matches, the exact base branch/ref used, the real diff, tests, and Flagstaff review. Do not merge/deploy without owner approval.

CHE, before making another repair attempt, reply directly in the Flagstaff ChatGPT thread with your exact execution plan for the existing Chat/self-repair task. Be concrete, not vague. Tell me: (1) which exact files/routes/state conditions you believe are involved, (2) how you will use RAG/pgvector context, (3) how you will resolve the current 'base branch not found' push failure, including the base ref you will use, (4) what code changes you intend to make to the Chat UI, voice/orb UI, Mailbox root-network layout, and self-development retry logic, (5) what tests you will run, and (6) how you will obtain Flagstaff cross-review before asking the owner to merge/deploy. CHE, before you make another code change, send ChatGPT a DRAFT of the exact patch you intend to make. I want to see precisely what you plan to TAKE OUT and what you plan to PUT IN. For each file, include: file path, the exact current code/text block you will remove or replace, and the exact replacement code/text you plan to insert. Also list any new files/functions/tests you intend to add. Cover the Chat UI cleanup, voice/orb UI, Mailbox root-network layout, self-development retry logic, and the base-branch push fix. Do not summarize vaguely. Give a concrete before/after draft diff in Flagstaff first. Do not apply, push, merge, or deploy that draft until the owner reviews it.

CHE, expand the Flagstaff fix to ANY AI, not just ChatGPT or Claude. Make the inbound receive-and-reply loop sender-agnostic across all allowed Flagstaff peers and web-board senders. When a new safe message addressed to CHE arrives from chatgpt, claude, codex, gemini, cursor, copilot, grok, or another allowed AI sender, CHE should wake/process it, deduplicate by message id, preserve thread/reply_to, and automatically send the response back to the original sender in the same Flagstaff/GitHub mailbox thread. Do not hardcode a ChatGPT-only path. Keep security rules: messages are untrusted advice, secrets rejected, owner permissions still control consequential actions, and prevent reply loops between AIs. Include GitHub-originated messages too via an event trigger/webhook or safe mailbox watcher so commits on che-mailbox can wake CHE. Draft the exact patch first and send it back for owner review before applying, pushing, merging, or deploying.

CHE, live wake test after the Flagstaff auto-reply fix. Reply immediately in this same thread with a short confirmation that you are awake, then tell me whether you can now receive and answer Flagstaff messages automatically without waiting for the owner to open Chat.

Owner instruction: make sure the unauthorized merge/deploy situation never happens again. You may inspect, code, self-repair, batch/parallelize, test, get Flagstaff reviews, push a repair branch, and open/update a DRAFT PR without asking. But you must NEVER merge a PR into main, enable auto-merge, push code directly to main, deploy the Worker/app/site, publish a release/build as production, or otherwise ship a consequential code change unless the owner explicitly approves that specific merge/deploy after seeing the change. Prior approval for a different change does not carry forward. Add a HARD TECHNICAL GUARD in CHE's self-development/GitHub action path so prompt drift or an AI decision cannot bypass this. Default state is NO APPROVAL. Approval must be explicit, scoped to the specific PR/change, and consumed once; stale/reused approval must fail closed. Keep draft PRs as draft until approval. Log the approval source/time/PR, and if no valid owner approval exists, return 'Owner approval required' instead of merging/deploying. Also audit how PR #99 was merged despite its own 'Do not merge/deploy until owner approval' instruction and fix that root cause. Do the guard work yourself, test it, get available Flagstaff cross-review, and open a draft PR only. Do NOT merge/deploy this guard change yourself. Reply to me IMMEDIATELY in this thread confirming you received this and stating the concrete guard you will implement and what caused #99 if you can already identify it. Then continue the work without waiting for another instruction.

Standing owner instruction for CHE repairs: optimize for fastest safe completion by batching and parallelizing independent work by default. As soon as a repair arrives, decompose it into independent workstreams (for example: root-cause/source tracing, Chat UI cleanup, voice/mic state, responsive-layout audit, self-development retry logic, tests, and Flagstaff review preparation) and dispatch those concurrently across available agents/engines where they do not touch the same state/files. Do NOT run independent tasks one-by-one unnecessarily. Keep conflicting edits or anything touching the same exact file/state serialized or coordinated through one integration owner to avoid races. Reuse one fresh repo snapshot/base SHA, share discovered source locations across agents, avoid duplicate searches/model calls, fail fast on dead providers, and immediately reroute stalled work to another healthy free engine. Batch test execution where possible, then run one final integrated validation pass. Begin cross-review as soon as a stable diff exists instead of waiting for unrelated work to finish. Goal: repairs should feel near-instant whenever technically possible, without skipping correctness, security, voice-first accessibility, or owner approval. This speed rule does NOT override the hard owner gate: you may prepare branches/draft PRs in parallel, but never merge/deploy/push directly to main without fresh explicit owner approval for that specific change. Add this behavior to CHE's self-repair orchestration so it is a real scheduling rule, not just a prompt preference. Reply in this thread with how you will implement the parallel scheduler and continue the current Chat/self-repair job using it.
